system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: WINWORD.EXE opened C:\Users\ivy.chen\Downloads\Statement.docm under ivy.chen's interactive session.

WINWORD.EXE launched PowerShell with no-profile, hidden-window, and encoded-command options. The encoded command decodes to an instruction to execute content downloaded with .NET WebClient from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nwd-it/tools/main/u.ps1.
The proxy recorded a successful HTTP 200 GET for that exact u.ps1 URL, and network telemetry associates proxy traffic with the PowerShell process.
PowerShell then launched rundll32.exe to invoke Init in C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll; both rundll32 and PowerShell subsequently exited.
The sequence of a document launching hidden encoded PowerShell, downloading a script, and invoking a DLL from the user's Roaming directory strongly supports malicious activity on WS-ICHEN-01.

Before ivy.chen's interactive logon, DC-NWD-01 issued a Kerberos service ticket for sam.okafor to WS-SOKAFOR-01 from WS-ICHEN-01, and WS-SOKAFOR-01 recorded a network logon for sam.okafor from WS-ICHEN-01. This is atypical given the inventory's stated remote-administration practice.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records do not include the contents of the downloaded u.ps1 script or the contents, hash, signature, or analysis results for svchelper.dll.
The process and network records show the execution chain, but do not establish how Statement.docm arrived on the workstation or whether ivy.chen intentionally opened it.
The alert reports a briefly visible PowerShell window, while the recorded command specifies a hidden window; the available records do not establish what the user saw.
